{{Quote|Thousands of meteor impacts an hour, ranging from microscopic to colossal. ''Perpetual bombardment.'' Each steps on its surface may be your last.|[[Lucien Draay]] describing the Rogue moon to a group of [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi Padawans]]|<ref name="KOTOR4">[[Knights of the Old Republic 4|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:Skyfall.png|thumb|right|280px|A meteor shower on a jungle world in the Kamdon system]]
A '''meteor''', also known as a '''shooting star''',<ref name="Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> was a form of object that entered a [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] from space.<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref> The [[Rogue Moon]] in the [[Taris system/Legends|Taris system]] sat in the middle of an [[Taris asteroid belt|asteroid field]], but had a retrograde orbit, traveling in the opposite direction of surrounding [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]]. As a result, it was bombarded heavily by meteors.<ref name="KOTOR4" /> 

A [[Unidentified jungle world (Kamdon system)|jungle world]] in the [[Kamdon system/Legends|Kamdon system]] experienced seasonal [[Meteor shower/Legends|meteor showers]] where meteors would enter the planet's atmosphere and tear through its surface, destroying untold acres of foliage, but also brought nutrients that the jungle needed to grow.<ref name="SW 30">[[Star Wars (1998) 30|''Star Wars'' (1998) 30]]</ref>

The [[Rishi moon|barren moon]] of [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]] was known to have meteor showers rain down onto the surface.<ref name="Rookies" /> The logo of the [[Meteor Cafe/Legends|Meteor Cafe]] featured a burning meteor and the name of the [[Restaurant/Legends|eatery]] in [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]].<ref name="Trivia">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/friends-and-enemies-trivia-gallery|text="Friends and Enemies" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 11}}</ref> The planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] had a lot of meteors; when the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] established a new [[Echo Station/Legends|secret base]] on the ice planet, all the meteor activity made it difficult to spot approaching [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="Episode V">{{Film|V}}</ref>

A common espionage tactic involved concealing [[Starship/Legends|starships]] within a mass of meteors. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the crew of ''[[Mon Remonda/Legends|Mon Remonda]]'' diverted a series of asteroids to create a meteor shower over [[Saffalore]] which provided cover for [[Wraith Squadron]]'s subsequent [[Mission to Saffalore|raid]]. When [[Elassar Targon]] was left on the roof of the [[Binring Biomedical Product]] facility with fellow [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] member [[Lara Notsil]], he spotted a shooting star and pointed out that seeing one meant good luck. However, Notsil was unsure if it was still considered good luck if the meteor was one of the asteroids that the squadron had just shot into the atmosphere.<ref name="Solo Command" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Meteors, meteorites and meteoroids===
In real life, the term meteor refers to the streak of light that appears in the sky when a ''[[Meteoroid/Legends|meteoroid]]''<ref name="Britannica What's">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/meteor|text=What's the Difference Between a Meteoroid, a Meteor, and a Meteorite?|author=Gregersen, Erik|quote='''A meteor is the streak of light''' that you see in the sky when a small piece of cometary or asteroidal material enters the atmosphere at high speed and burns up because of the frictional heating from the piece's collision with the atoms and molecules in the atmosphere. '''Before the small bit of comet or asteroid enters Earth's atmosphere, it floats through interplanetary space and is called a''' '''''meteoroid.'''''|work=''[[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|Encyclopædia Britannica]]''|archivedate=20230523235741}}</ref> (a lump of rock or [[Iron/Legends|iron]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around the [[Star/Legends|sun]])<ref name="National Geographic">{{WebCite|url=https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/meteoroid/|text=Meteoroid|quote=Meteoroids are lumps of rock or iron that orbit the sun, just as planets, asteroids, and comets do. (...) Most meteoroids are created from asteroid impacts. As asteroids crash and break up, their debris is classified as meteoroids.|work=[[Wikipedia:National Geographic|''National Geographic'']]|archivedate=20230519051742}}</ref> enters Earth's (or another [[Planet/Legends|planet's]]) [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] but burns up before it reaches the ground, which is why they're also called "shooting [[Star/Legends|stars]]." A ''[[Meteorite/Legends|meteorite]]'', on the other hand, is a meteoroid that enters the planet's atmosphere and survives the trip and hits the ground.<ref name="NASA">{{WebCite|url=https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/asteroids-comets-and-meteors/meteors-and-meteorites|text=What's the difference between a meteor, meteoroid, and meteorite?|quote='''Meteoroids''' are objects in space that range in size from dust grains to small asteroids. Think of them as "space rocks." When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere (or that of another planet, like Mars) at high speed and burn up, the fireballs or "shooting stars" are called '''meteors'''. When a meteoroid survives a trip through the atmosphere and hits the ground, it's called a '''meteorite'''.|work=[[Wikipedia:NASA|NASA]]|archivedate=20230423090620}}</ref> However, the terms meteoroid, meteor, and meteorite are sometimes used interchangeably in daily conversation.<ref name="Britannica and">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/meteor|text=meteor and meteoroid|quote=Meteoroids are believed to be mostly fragments of asteroids and comets and are placed, with them, in the category of solar system objects known as small bodies. A few meteoroids also have come from the Moon, Mars, Vesta, and possibly Mercury. The smallest meteoroids, those less than a few hundred micrometres across (about the size of a period on a printed page), are called interplanetary dust particles or micrometeoroids. The terms ''meteoroid'' and ''meteor'' (and meteorite as well) are sometimes confusingly interchanged in common usage. ''Meteor'' in particular is often applied to a meteoroid hurtling through space, to an incandescent meteoroid (rather than just its luminous streak) in the atmosphere, or to an object that has hit the ground or a human-made object. An example of the last case is found in the name Meteor Crater, a well-known impact structure in Arizona, U.S.|work=[[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|''Encyclopædia Britannica'']]|archivedate=20230307073411}}</ref>

===Meteoroids and asteroids===
Meteoroids range in size from tiny dust grains<ref name="NASA" /> to about 330 [[Foot/Legends|feet]] (100 [[Meter/Legends|meter]]s); space debris any bigger than this is considered an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]].<ref name="HowStuffWorks">{{WebCite|url=https://science.howstuffworks.com/question486.htm|text=How big does a meteor have to be to make it to the ground?|quote=Meteoroids have a pretty big size range. They include any space debris bigger than a molecule and smaller than about 330 feet (100 meters) -- space debris bigger than this is considered an '''asteroid'''.|work=[[Wikipedia:HowStuffWorks|HowStuffWorks]]|archivedate=20230325103739}}</ref>

Most meteoroids are fragments of asteroids and [[Comet/Legends|comets]] (although a few are known to come from other planets and [[Moon/Legends|moons]]),<ref name="Britannica and" /> explaining the high level of meteor activity on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in the film {{Film|V}}; the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]] is known to have a [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|dangerous asteroid field]]<ref name="Episode V" /> and most meteoroids are created from colliding asteroids.<ref name="National Geographic" /> 

===Linguistic confusion===
[[File:Meteor_strike.png|thumb|left|280px|The space rocks from the meteor shower in "Rookies" strike the surface, meaning that they're technically meteorites]]
People sometimes confuse meteoroid, meteor and meteorite since they are all used interchangeably in everyday language. The word "meteor" in particular is commonly used for a meteoroid flying through outer [[Realspace/Legends|space]], for a glowing meteoroid in the atmosphere (rather than just the burning streak of light in the sky), or for an object that has already landed on Earth (one example is found in the name [[Wikipedia:Meteor Crater|Meteor Crater]], a famous impact-structure in [[Wikipedia:Arizona|Arizona]]) or even a [[Human/Legends|human]]-made object.<ref name="Britannica and" />

This linguistic confusion has also spilled into ''Star Wars'' titles: For example, the meteors that enter the [[Unidentified jungle world (Kamdon system)|jungle world's]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] in the comic issue [[Star Wars (1998) 30|''Star Wars'' (1998) 30]] hit the planet's surface,<ref name="SW 30" /> meaning that is technically a ''[[Meteorite storm|meteorite shower]]'' rather than a [[Meteor shower/Legends|meteor shower]].<ref name="Britannica shower">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/meteor|text=meteorite shower|quote='''meteorite shower''', swarm of separate but related meteorites that land on Earth's surface at about the same time and place.|work=[[Wikipedia:Encyclopædia Britannica|''Encyclopædia Britannica'']]|archivedate=20230220121533}}</ref> In [[Knights of the Old Republic 4|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 4]], the space rocks that constantly bombard the surface of [[Rogue Moon|Rogue moon]] are referred to as meteors, but since they hit the surface rather than burn up,<ref name="KOTOR4" /> they are technically meteorites, not meteors.<ref name="NASA" /> The space rocks from the so-called meteor shower in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Rookies (episode)|Rookies]]" strike the surface of the [[Rishi moon]],<ref name="Rookies" /> meaning that they're technically meteorites.<ref name="NASA" />
